title: Strength

seo.title: Destiny matrix 11 — Strength: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: Strength, the eleventh arcanum of the destiny matrix, is about inner power and composure. What 11 means, how its strong version differs from the weak one.

meaning: The eleventh arcanum in the destiny matrix answers for inner strength — the kind that rests on reserves rather than on force. What eleven means is calm power that does not need to raise its voice to be heard. Such a person takes things not with a dash but with the ability to hold out longer than everyone else and not break where others have already given up.

The engine of this arcanum is taming, not crushing. On the card a woman gently closes a lion’s jaws: what is wild here is not killed but tamed — one’s own fear, one’s own anger, somebody else’s panic, a task nobody can lift. Hence the paradox of Strength: the calmer the person looks from outside, the more force they hold inside. Power here is measured not by what they can break, but by what they can bear and keep in check.

The main inner conflict of Strength is between “I will hold out” and “time to stop”. The very endurance that makes a person a support easily becomes a trap: if I bear it, then I can bear more — and a huge reserve goes for years into something that should have been let go long ago. Strength with no outlet does not disappear, it goes stale: unspent power turns into a dull weight the person carries about and takes for normal.

In its strong version the arcanum is a conscious support: the person spends the reserve where it is needed, knows how to say “enough” in time, and asks for help without counting that as weakness. The weak version is the silent strongman who drags everything alone, takes pride in it and slowly burns out, while all that power turns into pressure on the people nearby. The difference between them is not how much strength there is, but whether it has a direction and a brake.

From its neighbouring arcana the eleventh differs in the way it acts. The tenth, The Wheel, gives everything to chance and to the cycle — you are lucky or you are not; the eleventh does not wait for the turn, it endures every turn of the wheel and stays on its feet. The twelfth, The Hanged Man, lets go of control and looks at everything another way; the eleventh stays in the very thick of things and holds them up. Where one trusts to luck and the other gives in to the current, Strength simply endures — and by that alone it changes the situation.

article.title: Arcanum 11 in the destiny matrix: Strength that keeps a grip on itself
article.short: 11 in the destiny matrix is the arcanum Strength. It is the energy of a deep reserve and of command over yourself. A person with 11 has plenty of drive — anger, desire, competitive fire, stubbornness — and the task is neither to crush that drive nor to let it run loose, but to steer it. In the plus, Strength gives stamina, calm under pressure and influence without force: people listen to such a person, though they never raise their voice. In the minus it breaks in two directions — into pressure on others or into a clamp on yourself — and most often the two are one and the same loop. Below: how to find 11 from a date of birth, what it means in different points of the matrix, in the karmic tail and in a couple, and why Waite’s tarot numbers this card 8.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 11: the Strength arcanum — meaning, plus and minus
seo.description: Destiny matrix 11 is Strength: a deep reserve and command of your own drive. Two ways it breaks, 11 by birth date, tails, couples and why Waite numbers it VIII.

sections.h2: What 11 means: reserve, brake and soft power
paragraphs: Say “strength” and people picture muscle, push and a parade-ground voice. The eleventh arcanum is about something else: power that comes fitted with a brake. It has three layers, and Strength only happens when all three are working.

**The reserve.** The first thing 11 gives is fuel: energy, stamina, the ability to keep doing something hard for a long time without dropping out of the race. Waite’s divinatory list for this card opens with “power, energy, action, courage”. A person with pronounced Strength usually knows they last longer than others: through a second shift, through doing up the flat after work, through the project everyone else has walked away from.

**The brake.** A reserve on its own is not yet Strength. Strength begins where something powerful rises inside — rage, desire, fear, the thrill of the chase — and the person neither gives in to it nor pretends it isn’t there. They are furious and still speak evenly, because they have chosen where to send the anger. They want something badly and can wait. They are afraid, and they act. Waite described this card as a person’s higher nature getting the upper hand over the passions, and warned separately that it has “nothing to do with self-confidence in the ordinary sense”. Benebell Wen, author of Holistic Tarot, sets it apart from The Chariot in a single line: The Chariot is “the strength to master the world”, Strength is “strength to master the self”.

**Soft power.** The third layer is the least obvious: Strength does not work by pressure. Wen says so plainly — compassion and “gentle, subtle influence” instead of “brute force”. A person with 11 in the plus does not compel; they hold. They walk into a room where everyone is shouting, and ten minutes later people are talking, though they outshouted no one. Nobody argues with them — not out of fear, but because things get calmer when they are around.

Hence a simple test of whether someone has Strength or just a lot of energy: can they stop? Drop an argument they are winning. Abandon a task they are dragging on out of sheer stubbornness. Leave unsaid the sentence already on the tip of their tongue. Power without a brake is pressure. A brake without power is patience. Strength is having both.

sections.h2: Strength in the plus and in the minus: two ways to break, one vicious circle
paragraphs: In the plus, 11 is calm might. The person takes on a lot and carries it, without complaining or boasting. They get angry for good reason and out loud, want things fiercely and get them without breaking anyone. In hard times people lean on them, and they can take the weight.

Strength’s minus is built in an unusual way: it forks. All three authors we draw on describe this fork, although they are writing about different things. Among Waite’s reversed meanings stand despotism and abuse of power — and, right beside them, weakness. Wen has brute force and being “too stubborn and obstinate” or, the other way round, conduct that is “too passive”, a person holding back their own strength. For Yuliana Lisovskaya, who writes about compatibility, the minus of the eleventh energy is open aggression, or passivity and hidden, passive aggression.

head: What it looks like
What the person tells themselves
rows: **Strength in the plus**
Energy under control: anger voiced in time and in words, a load taken on that fits the strength, help asked for without shame
“I’m angry — and I’m going to say so, calmly, right now”
**Tipped outward: pressing**
A tone of command, arguing until they win, stubbornness on principle, flashes of rage, control over loved ones’ decisions and money, working to exhaustion as proof of power
“We’ll do it the way I said”
**Tipped inward: clamping**

No permission to be angry, to want or to be tired. The person hauls everything alone and says nothing, and the strength drains away into endurance, barbed remarks and a slammed door — or vanishes altogether: “I can’t make myself” on top of a huge reserve
“It’s fine, I’ll do it myself”

paragraphs: Most important of all: the two breakdowns are usually not two different people but two phases of the same one. First the clamp: six months of quietly finishing a colleague’s share of the work, never saying it hurts, never asking for anything. Then an explosion over a trifle — an unwashed mug, someone five minutes late — so violent that the whole office jumps. Next morning comes the shame, and the person promises themselves never to lose it again, which means enduring even harder. The circle closes, and with each turn the explosions come less often but louder.

What breaks the circle is not willpower — 11 has more than enough of that — but an early conversation. Anger voiced the day it appears weighs ounces. Anger carried for six months weighs a ton and no longer comes out as words.

paragraphs.h3: How to bring Strength back into the plus

ul: **Give the reserve a job.** 11 copes badly with idleness: unspent energy looks for a way out and finds it in irritation. It needs work where staying power belongs — a long project, a craft, training that takes real effort.
**Name your anger the same day.** In one sentence and without blame: “It got to me that…”. The sooner, the quieter.
**Ask yourself what you are enduring for, and until when.** Endurance with a goal and a deadline is Strength. Patience with no goal and no end date is a clamp.
**Ask, don’t push.** One direct request works better than three rounds of pressure. Caught yourself pushing? Ask what you actually want from the person.
**Check whose weight you are carrying.** Strength offers its shoulder before it has had time to think. Quite often a fair share of what a person with 11 is hauling isn’t theirs at all.

**Train the brake, not the engine.** 11 has power to spare. The exercise is to stop where you would usually push through: give way in an argument that doesn’t matter, finish work on time, put off a decision made in the heat of the moment.

sections.h2: How to find 11 from a date of birth
paragraphs: Strength is one of the most common arcana in the matrix. Somewhere in the full reading it turns up for 83.4% of people: only The Lovers, The Wheel of Fortune and Justice appear more often, and The Hierophant is level with it. Roughly one person in three (32.8%) has 11 in one of the five main points of the chart. But most often Strength hides deeper: it is in the chakra table for 57.2% of people and in the reading by decades for 43%.

The five main points are easy to check without a calculator. The matrix has a single reduction rule: any number above 22 is replaced by the sum of its digits until you get 22 or less. Anything from 1 to 22 stays as it is.

ul: **A, personality portrait or calling card** — 11 for anyone born on the 11th or the 29th (2 + 9 = 11).
**B, spiritual task** — 11 for everyone born in November.
**C, material task** — the sum of the digits of the year. Only 1901, 1910, 2009 and 2018 give 11, so adults almost never have Strength here: it belongs to children born in 2009 and 2018.
**D, karmic task** — add up A, B and C. A sum of 11, 29, 38, 47 or 56 reduces to 11. Example: 12.08.1971 — the year gives 1 + 9 + 7 + 1 = 18, the sum is 12 + 8 + 18 = 38, and 3 + 8 = 11.

**E, centre** — the sum of A, B, C and D. The centre will be 11 if A + B + C equals 19, 28, 37, 46 or 55. Example: 05.04.1981 — the year gives 1 + 9 + 8 + 1 = 19, the sum is 5 + 4 + 19 = 28, D = 10, centre 28 + 10 = 38 → 11.

paragraphs: The other points — the money, relationship and talent lines, the family line, purpose, the chakras — are built from these five, and they are easier to look up in the full calculation.

Two things often get confused here. First: in the matrix 11 is not reduced to 2. Numerology treats 11 as a “master number”, but the destiny matrix reduces only what is above 22, and 11 stays Strength. Second: repetition does not double an arcanum. Someone born on 12.08.1971 has 11 in the karmic task, in the talent line and in two decades running, from 50 to 70. That is not “double Strength” but one energy answering a different question in each point.

paragraphs.h3: Money: what Strength gets paid for

paragraphs: In the money line — the entry L, the money direction R2, which other schools’ charts call “under the dollar sign”, and the crossing R — 11 stands for 17.9% of people, and across the whole money section, earth total included, for 23.9%. Money comes here through endurance and effort: for work that is hard to keep up for long, for staying calm when everything is on fire, for the ability to lead people through a difficult stretch. Strength suits work that needs the body and stamina — sport, crafts, construction, manufacturing — and work that needs command of the situation: crisis management, negotiations, difficult clients.

The minus of money Strength is the same two breakdowns. Outward: money becomes an instrument of power, everything is controlled by one person, spending needs permission. Inward: the person takes on the heaviest projects at ordinary rates and mistakes being reliable for working for free. A separate trap is earning to the point of exhaustion to prove to yourself that you can take it.

paragraphs.h3: Decades and the arcanum of the year

paragraphs: In the reading by decades, age runs round the outer points of the chart: A — from birth to 10, F — from 10 to 20, B — from 20 to 30, G — from 30 to 40, C — from 40 to 50, H — from 50 to 60, D — from 60 to 70, I — from 70 to 80. So for everyone born in November the decade from 20 to 30 runs under Strength, and for those born on the 11th or the 29th the first ten years of life do. Such years are seldom light: life piles on responsibility and watches how the person handles it — carries it, presses others with it or wears themselves out.
If 11 has come up not in the chart but as the arcanum of the year, that is a different calculation and a different conversation — there is [a separate page on 11 for the year](/year/11).

The karmic tail is the three numbers of the matrix’s lower ray, running down from the centre. 11 can only be the last number of a tail: that is the karmic task D, the root of the tail. There are just two such tails, and which one is yours comes down to a single sum, A + B + C.

ul: **15-8-11** — when the sum is exactly 29. A tail about how a person handles power, their own and other people’s, when they sense a threat. The reading — [karmic tail 15-8-11](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-8-11).
**6-17-11** — when the sum is 11, 38, 47 or 56. A tail about a gift that did not disappear but was squandered. The reading — [karmic tail 6-17-11](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-17-11).

paragraphs: A tail ending in 11 belongs to 8.6% of people. In both cases Strength at the root is not a sentence but a direction: the tail leads towards taking your power in hand and spending it with intent.

sections.h2: 11 in compatibility: Strength in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: Compatibility in the destiny matrix is usually worked out not by comparing two charts but with a third one — the couple’s matrix. That is how Yuliana Lisovskaya works too, author of the book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (The Destiny Matrix: Compatibility): the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and reduced by the usual rule. One partner has 4 in the centre, the other 7 — the couple’s centre is 11. The method gives no compatibility percentages: it describes what holds the couple together and what trips it up.
What Strength means in a couple depends on the point:

ul: **The couple’s centre** — the atmosphere inside the union. The partners sense keenly what the other needs, charge each other up, and the tension between them goes into passion. In the minus — a fight for the upper hand, each with a truth of their own.

**The couple’s point A, the sum of the calling cards** — how others see the pair: energetic, focused, with a voice and weight, ringleaders and organisers. In the minus, outsiders can see who is in charge, and jibes at the partner are made even in company.

**The couple’s karmic task, point D** — what the couple has to master: handling aggression, respecting each other, sharing the housework fairly and saying from the very start what they like and what they don’t.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya’s advice to a couple with 11: keep a balance between work and family and between thrift and spending, don’t decide in the heat of the moment, be more physically active together and look at each other soberly, without rose-tinted glasses.

sections.h2: Arcanum 11 in a woman and in a man
paragraphs: The matrix calculation does not depend on sex: a man and a woman born on the same day have the same numbers, and 11 means the same thing for both. What differs is not the arcanum but how other people meet the way it shows itself.

A woman with vivid Strength more often hears “tone it down” and “you take too much on yourself”. Hence two familiar reactions: hide the power and become easy to live with — or prove it by hauling everything alone, “because there’s nobody else”. A man with the same Strength more often hears “men don’t complain”, and a ban on tiredness and fear comes to feel normal. Both roads lead to the same breakdown — the clamp, followed sooner or later by an explosion. And the way out is the same for both: allow yourself to be angry, to be tired and to ask — out loud and in good time.

If 11 belongs to someone close to you, living alongside them is easier when you remember three things. Don’t pit your strength against theirs head-on: Strength can withstand pressure for a long time, but it responds at once to respect and a direct request. Don’t take a long silence for agreement — more often it is a build-up. And don’t leave their energy without work: with nothing to carry, Strength goes sour and turns into irritation.

sections.h2: How Strength differs from The Chariot, Justice, The Devil and The Emperor

ul: **The Chariot, 7.** Strength aimed outward: to win, to get there, to take. 11 is aimed inward: to master yourself. The Chariot asks how to win; Strength asks how not to lose yourself while you are winning. Together they give drive without breakdowns — [The Chariot and Strength](/encyclopedia/combination/7-11).

**Justice, 8.** Strength swapped numbers with it in Waite’s deck, which is why the two are confused all the time. Justice weighs things up and answers for the consequences; Strength endures and holds steady. More on the eighth arcanum — [Justice](/encyclopedia/arcanum/8).

**The Devil, 15.** The same raw material — passion, desire, the thrill of the chase — but with the opposite sign: in The Devil desire leads the person, in Strength the person leads desire. When the two meet in one chart — [Strength and The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/11-15).

**The Emperor, 4.** Power through order: rules, structure, control over circumstances and people. The power of Strength gets by without controlling anyone else — it rests on calm and on its own self-command. Together — [The Emperor and Strength](/encyclopedia/combination/4-11).

sections.h2: Strength in Waite’s tarot: the picture, the number VIII and the divinatory meanings
paragraphs: The classic card comes from the Rider–Waite–Smith deck: Pamela Colman Smith drew it to Arthur Edward Waite’s design, and the deck came out in 1909. A woman in a white dress, with a wreath of flowers on her head, bends over a lion and closes its jaws. A garland of flowers circles her and runs on to the lion — Waite himself calls it a chain of flowers. Above the woman’s head floats a figure eight lying on its side, the sign of infinity, the same one as above The Magician. Around her is green earth, in the distance a blue mountain, and the sky is yellow.

Waite stressed that his design differs from the conventional ones in one point only: “her beneficent fortitude has already subdued the lion, which is being led by a chain of flowers”. In one aspect the lion signifies the passions, and the woman is “the higher nature in its liberation”. The chain of flowers is “the sweet yoke and the light burden of Divine Law, when it has been taken into the heart of hearts”; here Waite all but repeats the Gospel line “my yoke is easy, and my burden is light”. The passions are neither killed nor locked in a cage: they are led, and led not by force but by what the heart has taken in.

On self-confidence Waite was blunt: the card “has nothing to do with self-confidence in the ordinary sense”; it concerns “the confidence of those whose strength is God”. Next comes a line lifted almost word for word from a psalm: “It has walked upon the asp and the basilisk and has trodden down the lion and the dragon.” Waite names two more meanings separately — inviolate innocence (in Latin, innocentia inviolata) and “the strength which resides in contemplation”. These higher meanings, he cautions, are “matters of inference” and are not “transparent on the surface of the card”.

The figure itself is older than Waite. Strength is one of three virtues among the major arcana, along with Justice and Temperance; in the book Waite calls it “Strength, or Fortitude”. Early Italian cards showed it in different ways: in the Visconti–Sforza deck a youth, often read as Hercules, raises a club over a lion; on other cards a woman holds or breaks a stone column. The Tarot de Marseille settled on the woman with the lion: she calmly opens the beast’s jaws, and the brim of her wide hat curves into something like the infinity sign. Waite knew both gestures — opening the jaws and closing them — and thought the closing hand “better symbolically”, though either one “conveys the idea of mastery”.

In Waite’s deck the number is VIII, not XI. He swapped Strength and Justice himself and declined to explain, “for reasons which satisfy myself”; as the change “carries nothing with it which will signify to the reader”, he added, there was no cause for explanation. It is usually linked to the Golden Dawn, the order that matched the major arcana to the signs of the zodiac: the eighth card got Leo, the eleventh Libra. The destiny matrix keeps the older, Marseille order: 11 is Strength, 8 is Justice. So in books and on websites that follow Waite, our arcanum 11 is described under the number VIII, while XI there is Justice. The change Waite did not think worth explaining has become the main source of confusion around this card for anyone who reads the matrix.

For divination Waite gives the card these meanings. Upright: “Power, energy, action, courage, magnanimity; also complete success and honours.” Reversed: “Despotism, abuse of power, weakness, discord, sometimes even disgrace.” The destiny matrix has no reversed cards: the number is calculated from the date, and the plus and minus of 11 are not the position of a card but the way a person handles their own strength.
